blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the top of the negotiation stack, payment terms are rarely discussed in isolation. They sit inside a package that also includes pricing, volume commitments, duration, service levels, performance guarantees, and sometimes strategic concessions that are not written down anywhere. The discussion is between adults who know, without saying it, that everything trades against everything else.

In this environment, a good negotiator does not argue about days of credit. She frames the conversation around the total cost of the relationship over time: what do you really need, what can we accept, and what would both sides still be comfortable with if volumes doubled or halved?

The language matters. At this level, negotiators use the subjunctive almost instinctively — "I would suggest that we consider a phased structure"; "I recommend that the committee review the exposure before signing." The register is softer, the stakes are higher, and the discipline is to leave room for both sides to move without losing face. Deals at this level often take longer to agree — and then last for years.

items.q: According to the text, why are payment terms rarely discussed in isolation?
options: They form part of a wider package where every variable trades against the others
They are decided by lawyers rather than negotiators
They are considered too trivial to raise
They are fixed by regulation and cannot be moved
items.why: "They sit inside a package… everything trades against everything else." Termos de pagamento fazem parte de um pacote maior.

items.q: How does the skilled negotiator frame the conversation?
options: Around the number of days of credit
Around the total cost of the relationship over time
Around the current market price only
items.why: "She frames the conversation around the total cost of the relationship over time."

items.q: The stress-test question "if volumes doubled or halved?" suggests that the author values…
options: agreements that only work under today's exact conditions
terms that both sides can still live with if circumstances change
locking the counterparty into a single volume forever
items.why: Inferência: o teste de dobrar/reduzir volume mostra que a autora valoriza acordos robustos a mudanças de cenário.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The best move is to win the argument over days of credit
Strategic concessions may never appear in the written contract
A softer register can coexist with higher stakes
Slow deals at this level tend to be durable
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz explicitamente que um bom negociador NÃO discute dias de crédito — logo discordaria de 'ganhar essa discussão'.

items.q: Why, according to the text, do negotiators reach for the subjunctive at this level?
options: Because it is grammatically required in contracts
Because a softer register leaves both sides room to move without losing face
Because it speeds the deal up
Because it hides the real terms from the committee
items.why: "The register is softer… leave room for both sides to move without losing face." O subjuntivo suaviza o tom.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver conduzindo a negociação com a refinaria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. Six months in, I think we're close, so let me be candid about where I sit. I would suggest that we stop treating payment terms as a separate battle. They aren't. Credit days, the volume commitment, the duration — they all move together, and if we pull one, the others shift.

Here's my proposal. I recommend that we consider a phased structure: tighter terms in year one while both sides build confidence, then a gradual loosening as the relationship proves itself. If your board would rather anchor the pricing first, that's fine — but I'd ask that the pricing and the volume commitment be discussed in the same room, on the same afternoon. They can't be split.

On the service levels, we have some room to give. On the performance guarantee, frankly, less. What I would not want is for either of us to walk away feeling we were pushed into something we can't defend internally.

So my recommendation is simple: let's agree the shape of the package this week, and leave the fine print to the committees. If we get the shape right, this deal lasts a decade. If we haggle line by line, it lasts until the first surprise.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Oliver suggest they stop doing?
options: Treating payment terms as a separate battle
Meeting so frequently with the board
Offering any concessions on service levels
items.why: "I would suggest that we stop treating payment terms as a separate battle."

items.q: What is the phased structure Oliver proposes?
options: Tighter terms in year one, loosening gradually as trust builds
Identical terms for the full duration
items.why: "tighter terms in year one while both sides build confidence, then a gradual loosening."

items.q: On which point does Oliver signal he has the LEAST room to give?
items.why: "On the service levels, we have some room to give. On the performance guarantee, frankly, less."

items.q: When Oliver insists pricing and the volume commitment be discussed "in the same room, on the same afternoon," he implies that…
options: the two variables are linked and cannot be negotiated separately
he wants the meeting to finish quickly
the board is not allowed to see the pricing
volume no longer matters to the deal
items.why: Inferência: fazer questão de tratá-los juntos mostra que preço e volume estão amarrados — não podem ser separados.

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "If we haggle line by line, it lasts until the first surprise"?
options: A deal fought over detail is fragile and will break at the first shock
The contract must list every line item
Surprises are good for the relationship
The committees should handle every clause personally
items.why: Inferência: ele contrapõe 'acertar a forma do pacote' (dura uma década) a 'brigar linha por linha' (quebra no primeiro imprevisto).

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We're negotiating with an institutional counterparty, not a family firm." Institutional here means…
options: belonging to a large, established organisation with formal governance
acting on impulse and without records
items.why: Institutional = institucional: uma organização grande e estabelecida, com governança formal.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I'd rather ___ the discussion around total cost than argue about credit days."
items.why: To frame = enquadrar: dar o recorte/ângulo da conversa.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "They accepted the price only because we offered a five-year ___."
items.why: Volume commitment = compromisso de volume: o que foi oferecido em troca do preço.

items.q: "We agreed a phased structure to spread the risk." A phased structure is…
options: an arrangement rolled out in stages rather than all at once
a fixed price with no flexibility
items.why: Phased structure = estrutura em fases: implementada por etapas para diluir o risco.

items.q: "At this level the register is deliberately soft." In this context register means…
options: the style and level of formality of the language used
items.why: Register = registro (de linguagem): o grau de formalidade e o tom das palavras escolhidas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em negociações de alto nível. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on the phased structure." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Their board pushed back on the performance guarantee." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the shape this week and will hammer out the fine print later." To hammer out means to…
options: work out the details through hard discussion
items.why: Hammer out = martelar/negociar os detalhes até chegar a um acordo definitivo.

items.q: "Both sides want to save face, so leave them room to move." To save face means to…
items.why: Save face = salvar a face: evitar humilhação ou perda de prestígio na frente do outro lado.

items.q: "If we get the shape right, the deal will hold up for a decade." To hold up means to…
options: remain valid and durable over time
items.why: Hold up = aguentar/sustentar-se: o acordo permanece firme e válido ao longo do tempo.
